beats.beat: At Jasper's homestead, Elin spots racks of leaves with bright silver veins that smear faintly when she rubs her thumb across them.
Garret confirms it is berry dye painted over unripe veins, not true silvering.
Cornered, Jasper admits the mature trees nearby are stripped bare from years of cutting, and he started painting the veins to make quota and pay for his mother's medicine.
A neighbor runs up with the news that the shipment already left before dawn, loaded onto Kettering's buyer caravan bound for Tollgate, a full day's lead ahead of them.

turn.note: Chapter ends on the caravan's full-day head start, forcing an immediate chase that sets up chapter 4.

problems: A narrator segment reads only 'said Elin.' immediately after a segment already tagged speaker Elin Hargrove, duplicating the attribution for no reason.
'Jasper Lund stood in it with a bucket in one hand' leaves 'it' ambiguous between the lifted sack and the doorway it reveals; a listener cannot resolve this on the fly.

listenability: The redundant 'said Elin.' narrator line after an already-tagged Elin segment is dead weight and should be cut or merged into the preceding line.
'Jasper Lund stood in it' has an unclear antecedent for 'it' (sack vs. doorway); rewrite as 'Jasper Lund stood in the gap' or similar.
trope_note: Serves the apprentice (Elin's thumb test) and the rule that must not be broken (Jasper's dyed veins) directly; the thing nobody has studied is reserved for chapter 4 as planned, so no fourth trope creeps in here.
fixes: Cut the stray narrator segment 'said Elin.' following the already-tagged Elin Hargrove line; it duplicates the attribution and adds nothing.
Rewrite 'Jasper Lund stood in it with a bucket in one hand' so 'it' clearly names the doorway or gap, not the lifted sack.

Consider trimming one of the two consecutive Jasper speeches ('There isn't a tree old enough...' and 'Nine doesn't pay a carter...') to tighten the confession, since both make the same point about insufficient yield.
